summary: This joint resolution terminates the national emergency that the President declared on February 1, 2025, in Executive Order 14193.

scores.thoughts: The bill text terminates a national emergency declared by executive order but contains no provisions, authorizations, or changes related to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budgetary authority. It has no bearing on government spending.
The resolution addresses only the termination of a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act and makes no reference to tax policy, rates, deductions, or revenue measures.
No provisions in the bill text relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market structures.
The bill does not address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues in any way.
Although the underlying emergency might concern border or immigration matters, the bill text itself contains no immigration-related language, policy changes, or enforcement provisions.
No content in the resolution pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill terminates an unspecified national emergency but includes no language altering defense spending, military authorities, or Department of Defense operations.
The resolution has no provisions concerning environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resource management.
No references to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net funding appear in the bill text.
The bill does not engage with education policy, school funding, or federal involvement in schooling.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance regulation.
The resolution contains no language on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal-justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are present in the bill.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The text includes no provisions affecting LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
No foreign-aid authorizations or reductions are mentioned.
The resolution does not touch on voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No data-privacy, technology-regulation, or surveillance provisions appear in the bill.
The bill contains no labor, union, or workplace-policy content.
No language addresses religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination rules.
